interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several factors, including a preoperative PSA of 25 and an ISUP grade group 3 pathology from the prostatectomy specimen. Contributing to risk are the presence of extraprostatic extension and positive surgical margins. Conversely, favorable findings include no seminal vesicle invasion, absence of lymphovascular invasion, and no documented lymph node metastasis. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy comparison shows a difference in Gleason grading (4+4 at biopsy vs. 4+3 at prostatectomy). Missing information regarding the postoperative PSA trajectory would significantly impact prognosis assessment. Further follow-up data on PSA levels are necessary to refine risk stratification beyond the current findings. The fixed estimated horizon is 42.09 months. This is a predicted recurrence horizon, not evidence of observed recurrence. The sensitivity range is 33.67–50.51 months; its coverage has not been validated.
